name: Bosch EDC15C6 (Mercedes CDI, CR1 / CR2)
flash_note: Flash chip by hardware revision: a 29F400 (512 KiB; the chip of the sibling VAG EDC15P in the cited boot-mode post) or a 29F800 (1 MiB; OpenTune's edc15c6 checksum is validated on 1 MiB images). Confirm from the chip marking on your board before reading.

read_methods.notes: Diagnostics run over K-line KWP2000 (ISO 14230). OpenTune's own clean-room bench work on an owner unit confirmed the datalink (5-baud wake address 0x12, key bytes EF 8F, W4 about 40 ms, separate-length-byte frame form; see access.obd). A COMPLETE read or a write over the diagnostic socket is NOT validated: it needs the ECU's security access, and the programming-session unlock is unproven on-unit (access.security). The proven full-read paths are the board-level C167 bootstrap loader (access.boot) and a bench read; OBD read/write capability is left unknown until validated.

notes: First-generation Mercedes common-rail CDI (Mercedes calls the ECU CR1.x / CR2.x). Part numbers are Mercedes prefixes per engine (A611.../A612.../A613...). Checksum: OpenTune's edc15c6 module verifies and corrects the Mercedes 1 MiB block chain (validated on real stock and tuned dumps); unrecognised images are refused. Ground pin is disputed between sources (see bench.notes).

pins.note: Disputed: ecupinouts gives ground on 1-6 instead. Do not wire without checking continuity.
Disputed: Transpondery gives ground on 1-5 instead. Do not wire without checking continuity.
ecupinouts lists 1-8 as the second +12 V pin instead; single conflicting source.
Transpondery lists 1-7 as the second terminal-15 pin instead; single conflicting source.

bench.notes: Supply (2-13 terminal 30, 1-1 terminal 15) and K-line (3-28) agree between sources. The GROUND pin is deliberately left out: Transpondery says 1-5, ecupinouts says 1-6. Identify ground on your unit by continuity to the housing/other ground pins before powering.
bench.resistor_notes: K-line programming; CAN termination not needed for it.

safety_note: Bench safety: use a current-limited bench supply (12-13.8 V, start with a low current limit) and a fuse in the +12 V lead; connect ground first. Confirm every pin with a multimeter on YOUR unit before applying power - ground pins should show continuity to each other (and usually the housing), and hardware revisions can differ from the sources. A CAN bus needs about 60 ohm between CAN-H and CAN-L (two 120 ohm terminations): add a 120 ohm resistor if neither the unit nor your interface terminates. Swapped CAN-H/CAN-L just gives timeouts; +12 V on a signal pin can destroy the unit.

Infineon SAK-C167CR-LM errata sheet: CPU.7 warm hardware reset shorter than 1032 TCL
AMD Am29F800B data sheet: 44-pin SO, DQ4 = pin 24
OBD2Express blog (retailer post): reading a VAG EDC15P (29F400) in boot mode, flash pin 24 to ground at power-up
OpenTune docs/C167-BSL.md: C167 bootstrap-mode read on EDC15 (sequence, strap, K-line link)
ISO 14230-2 (KWP2000 data link layer): 5-baud initialisation, key-byte handshake, W1-W4 inter-byte timing
ISO 14230-4 (KWP2000 for emissions-related systems): functional legislated-OBD addressing (0x33)

OpenTune docs/DRIVERS.md section 3l (K-line): own clean-room EDC15C6 datalink facts - 5-baud wake 0x12, key bytes EF 8F, W4 ~40 ms (25-50 ms), separate-length-byte frame form, no legislated OBD at 0x33

obd.protocol: KWP2000 (ISO 14230) on the K-line, connector pin 3-28. Datalink (OpenTune own-unit clean-room): 5-baud initialisation at address 0x12, key bytes EF 8F, W4 inter-byte timing about 40 ms (25-50 ms window), and a separate-length-byte frame form (80 12 F1 <len> ...). No legislated-OBD responder at functional address 0x33 (manufacturer diagnostics only).
obd.notes: The K-line pin agrees between both pinout sources. CONFIRMED live over OBD/K-line by OpenTune's own clean-room bench work (own unit): the datalink (identify 1A 86 + own-dump analysis; the generic 5-baud / key-byte / W4 mechanism is ISO 14230-2/-4, documented in docs/DRIVERS.md section 3l) AND default-session diagnostic/identification reads (service 1A) after the default-session 2-byte unlock. UNVALIDATED over OBD: a COMPLETE calibration/flash read (it needs the unproven programming-session key) and any write. So obd.mode is 'unknown' about a full read/write, NOT about the bus - the link and diagnostic reads are live; the proven full-read paths are boot (C167 BSL) and bench.

bench.how: On the desk through the three connector blocks: terminal 30 on 2-13, terminal 15 on 1-1, K-line on 3-28 (both sources agree). Ground is disputed (1-5 or 1-6): find it by continuity before powering. Same protocol and security access as in the car.

boot.mcu_mode: C167-family bootstrap loader (BSL) on ASC0 (RxD0 = P3.11, TxD0 = P3.10), 8N1: after reset the host sends one zero byte, the BSL takes its baud rate from it and answers with an identification byte (C5h = C167 derivatives, D5h = devices with identification registers), then loads exactly 32 bytes of loader code. On EDC15 boards ASC0 reaches the K-line through the board's transceiver.

points.name: Flash DQ4 to CPU P0L.4/AD4
points.note: Only valid if the board routes flash DQ4 to CPU AD4 (C167CR P-MQFP-144 pin 104 = P0L.4/AD4): confirm continuity between flash pin 24 and CPU pin 104 before using it. The C167CR manual's example pull-down on P0L.4 is 8 kOhm.

boot.reset_timing: P0L.4 must read low at the end of the hardware reset: apply the pull-down before power-up and release it once the BSL has answered (the cited EDC15P post releases after about 5 s; OpenTune's notes cite 2-3 s). P0L.5, P0L.3 and P0L.2 must read high (Table 19-2: P0L.5..2 = 1 0 1 1 selects the standard bootstrap loader). A hardware reset pulse must last at least 1032 TCL (errata CPU.7).
boot.notes: Board level only: the case has to be opened. No public source documents this route for the EDC15C6 itself: the C167 bootstrap loader is the EDC15 platform's, and grounding flash pin 24 at power-up is reported for the sibling VAG EDC15P in a retailer blog post. Check the CPU marking (C167 family) and the flash chip on your board first. OpenTune's BSL read only reads; it never writes or erases.

security.notes: KWP2000 SecurityAccess (service 0x27) gates diagnostics. From OpenTune's own clean-room bench work, two scheme CLASSES are noted (classes only - no formulas, constants or keys are published, and OpenTune ships no OEM key): (1) a DEFAULT-session 2-byte seed/key (27 01 / 27 02), access at this level is live-validated on an owner unit but its derivation is kept private; (2) a PROGRAMMING-session unlock reached after StartDiagnosticSession 10 85, of the form 4-byte seed -> 8-byte key - this one is NOT confirmed on-unit (unproven), so a complete read or programming over OBD is not validated. Use your own key through the off-by-default seed/key loader, or the board-level boot read, which runs before the ECU software and needs no key.
